title: Adding an X-Iceberg-Client-Capabilities header to the REST spec
summary: singhpk234 proposed a generic X-Iceberg-Client-Capabilities header (PR #16394) sent on catalog requests so that a client can declare which features it understands, such as vended-credentials, remote-signing and scan-planning, with read-restrictions to follow. The header is a forward-compatibility hint, not a security mechanism. sungwy supported it and asked whether capability values need versioning; the author replied that a fail-closed rule makes versions unnecessary. danielcweeks preferred feature-specific headers on the endpoints where they apply, and later listed concerns: capabilities depend on engine and configuration, a global header does not say which endpoints are targeted, and capabilities may proliferate. He and rdblue suggested that a versioned v2 loadTable endpoint is the existing way to introduce forward-breaking changes and should be considered instead. RussellSpitzer saw no reason a generic header must be sent on every request. The thread ends with the v2 endpoint suggestion and no decision.

positions.stance: A single generic capabilities header with an enum of values is a static advertisement of what the client understands and is easy to extend.
Supports a generic header for compatibility and response shaping, and asks whether capability values should be versioned contracts.
A generic header does not require sending every capability with every request; clients could send only the relevant ones per endpoint.
A global capabilities header adds complexity that is not narrowly targeted; a v2 loadTable endpoint should be examined instead.
Versioned endpoints are the existing way to introduce forward-breaking changes, so a v2 loadTable endpoint is cleaner than either header approach.

outcome.note: No agreement. The author reported that the 26 May sync leaned towards a generic header, while danielcweeks and rdblue proposed considering a v2 loadTable endpoint instead.

why_it_matters: The choice between a capabilities header and a v2 loadTable endpoint decides how clients opt into forward-breaking REST features such as read restrictions.
